title: AEM violation tickets: the Violation Tickets page, drawer, split and merge, comments and activity log

prose.label: The drawer.
prose.text: {{drawer-role}} {{comments-attachments}} {{activity-log}} The drawer's tab contents are open {{gap:drawer-tabs}}, and so are the role permissions for tickets {{gap:ticket-permissions}}.

prose.label: Split and merge.
prose.text: {{split}} {{merge}} Grouping rule sets are in [[aem.ticket-grouping-rules]], and statuses and workflows in [[aem.ticket-lifecycle]].

definition.statement: An AEM violation ticket aggregates related policy violations into a single work item, and tickets can be dispatched to external platforms such as Jira or ServiceNow.

quotes: Each violation ticket aggregates related policy violations into a single work item
Dispatch violation tickets to external platforms (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow) to streamline workflows and remediation processes.

active-view-filters.statement: On the Violation Tickets page the Active view is the system default and shows all violation tickets with at least one active policy violation; tickets can be filtered by Severity, State, Assignee or Policy Violation Count.

quotes: The Active view is the system default, which displays all violation tickets with at least one active policy violation.
Filter violation tickets by Severity, State, Assignee, or Policy Violation Count.

bulk-actions.statement: Bulk actions on selected violation tickets are Update, Merge and Create 3rd party Issue, and the ticket list can be exported as a CSV file.

quotes: Update: Update the details of a group of selected violation tickets.
Merge: Merge multiple selected tickets into one violation ticket.
Create 3rd party Issue: Dispatch a group of selected violation tickets to external work management systems.
Export the list of violation tickets and their associated details as a CSV file.

columns.statement: With the default Active saved view, a violation ticket shows a Severity Score calculated from the severity scores of its policy violations (for example the highest or the average), an SLA deadline, and a Remediation percentage of policy violations resolved.

quotes: When the default Active saved view is selected, you can see the following details for each violation ticket:

Severity Score: The severity score assigned to the violation ticket, calculated based on the severity scores of the policy violations within the violation ticket (e.g., using the highest score or the average score).
SLA: The service-level agreement (SLA) deadline for the violation ticket.
Remediation: The percentage of policy violations resolved within the violation ticket.

drawer-role.statement: The actions available in the violation ticket drawer depend on the user role in AEM, and Apply Changes is clicked after updating the ticket.

quotes: The actions you can perform in the violation ticket drawer depend on your user role in AEM.
Click Apply Changes after making updates to the violation ticket.

split.statement: Policy violations can be split from a violation ticket into one new ticket or a separate ticket per violation; at least one selected policy violation must be active and inactive selections cannot be split, and the original ticket is listed on the Related Tickets tab of the new ticket.

quotes: You can split policy violations from a violation ticket into one or more new tickets.
At least one of the selected policy violations must be active; inactive selections cannot be split.
Split Into a New Violation Ticket: Split all policy violations into one ticket.
Split Into <#> New Violation Tickets: Create separate tickets for each policy violation.
You can view the original ticket from which policy violations were split on the Related Tickets tab of your newly created ticket.

merge.statement: Selected violation tickets can be merged into a single ticket, for example when tickets contain similar policy violations resolved by the same fix; the merge dialog takes an Assignee and a Status for the new ticket.

quotes: A common use case for merging violation tickets is when multiple violation tickets contain similar policy violations that can be resolved with the same fix.
Assignee: Enter the name of the user responsible for reviewing or resolving the violation ticket.
Status: Select a status for the new ticket (e.g., New, Open, In Progress, etc.).

comments-attachments.statement: A violation ticket has a Comments tab for comments and an Add Attachment icon to attach supporting evidence to a comment.

quotes: Click the Comments tab.
This enables the security team to attach evidence related to the policy violation, providing additional context and making the violation easier to review.
Click the Add Attachment icon and add the required attachment.

activity-log.statement: A violation ticket's Activity tab is an audit trail of status changes, assignment changes, ticket updates and system-recorded events, with who performed each action and when.

quotes: The Activity tab displays the history of actions performed on the violation ticket.
It provides an audit trail of violation ticket activities such as status changes, assignment changes, ticket updates, system-recorded events, who performed each action, and when each action occurred.

severity-score-formula.title: Which formula an account uses for a violation ticket's severity score
severity-score-formula.detail: The page gives only "e.g., using the highest score or the average score" for how a ticket's severity score is calculated from its policy violations; which one an account uses is not stated.

ticket-permissions.title: Which role permissions gate violation tickets, ticket workflows and AEM dashboards
ticket-permissions.detail: The ticket pages say drawer actions depend on the user role in AEM; unlike Policies (Assets App > Policy Rule), they name no permission resource for tickets, the Violation Ticket Lifecycle workflows or the dashboards.

drawer-tabs.title: What the violation ticket drawer tabs contain
drawer-tabs.detail: The drawer page lists Top Panel, Details, Policy Violations and Assets but shows only an image placeholder; the fields in each are not captured. The Comments, Activity and Related Tickets tabs are named only on other pages, so which tabs the drawer has in all is not stated.
